method: Free WebSearch + WebFetch article reads (no paid models, no Supabase, no X/Gemini). Takeaways are PARAPHRASED and attributed; WebFetch extraction is not reliable for verbatim quotes, so none are stored. Claims were cross-checked against data/fantasy/boxscores/espn-*.json; contradicted claims were dropped (listed in rejected).

takeaways.text: Ward INT sparked 21 unanswered CLE points; Rodgers tied it 24-24 to Freiermuth at 1:44; Szmyt 56-yd FG with 10s left. CLE 3-1, best start since 2021; Watson's third straight 4th-quarter comeback.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: CLE B+: Watson keeps playing well, rookies Boston and Concepcion 9-153 combined, five sacks. PIT B-: Rodgers 299 yds but two ill-advised INTs, Boswell's third missed FG, defense keeps giving up big plays.

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: PIT receivers created separation on only ~14.7% of routes, forcing Rodgers into near-perfect throws; CLE rookie WRs established as real targets.

takeaways.author: Jeremy Bergman
takeaways.text: Taylor (95 yds, 2 TD) steadied IND after early Jones turnovers. WSH lost Mariota (MCL) to 7th-round rookie Kaliakmanis. Sauce Gardner had his worst career game (117 yds on 5 targets, burned for a 47-yd Burks TD).

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: IND B but scoreline flattering: Jones 55.9% with an INT and fumble; Taylor and defense carried it vs a third-string QB. WSH C: kept it close into the 4th.

takeaways.author: Stephen Holder, John Keim
takeaways.text: IND winning ugly; Buckner dominant post-neck surgery. WSH injury list (Daniels, Tunsil, McLaurin, Cosmi, Mariota) is the story.

takeaways.author: Nick Shook
takeaways.text: NYG defense won it: goal-line stand plus Deonte Banks' 98-yd pick-six. ARI blew a 14-3 lead, punted three times in the 4th and failed at the goal line. Winston: 3 TD, 2 INT on consecutive 2nd-half drives.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: ARI C: Brissett's first 3-INT game in 11 years, ending with the pick-six at the NYG 4. NYG B: second straight week the defense won the game.

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: Marvin Harrison Jr. clearly behind McBride and Wilson (1 catch on 4 targets).

takeaways.author: Kevin Patra
takeaways.text: Lamb 17-189-1, 11-140-1 in the 2nd half; Dak targeted him on 21 of 45 routes. HOU defense collapsed; Javonte Williams scored three short TDs. Collins returned for 2 TDs.
Loser: DeMeco Ryans/HOU defense. CB Kamari Lassiter allowed 136 yds on 50 snaps with three penalties, most allowed by a CB this season. Stroud is playing well; the defense is the problem.
HOU gave up 28 second-half points and fell to 0-4 despite Stroud's 347 yds.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: DAL B (Prescott's game-winning 12-yd TD with 40s left); HOU B-: defense couldn't slow Dallas.

takeaways.author: Bobby Kownack
takeaways.text: GB escaped: penalties on the first play of four drives, 2-of-9 on 3rd down. Love has 2 TD passes in every game (matches his 2020 pace). TB forced late turnovers off rookie Jalon Daniels' first start; Edgerrin Cooper hurt (Achilles).

takeaways.author: Rob Demovsky, Jenna Laine
takeaways.text: GB had 4th-quarter turnovers at the TB 1 and 7. Daniels showed promise despite 2 INTs; Mayfield (thumb) out.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: GB C: ugliest win of the week; offense out of sync. TB C: hard to win with an undrafted rookie QB; 0-4.

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: GB RBs Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd both fumbled.

takeaways.author: Nick Shook
takeaways.text: JAX won through ~100 first-half penalty yards by taking away two Burrow INTs (one set up a TD, the second ended a 4th-quarter red-zone drive). The JAX formula is a credible run game plus turnover-free Lawrence.

takeaways.author: Michael DiRocco, Ben Baby
takeaways.text: JAX has 10 takeaways in 4 games but its secondary is getting hurt. Burrow has 13 4th-quarter/OT turnovers since the start of 2024.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: CIN C+: 428 pass yds but the run game was nonexistent; late Burrow decisions cost it.

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: Ja'Marr Chase left with a concussion; Gesicki and Tinsley stepped up as Burrow threw for 428.

takeaways.author: Jeremy Bergman
takeaways.text: LAR came back from 20-10 with 14 unanswered (Kyren go-ahead TD; Nacua 9-125). PHI 0-for-12 on 3rd down, most attempts without a conversion since 1991; Hurts 93 yds. PHI lost Barkley, Greenard, Q. Mitchell and Bigsby in-game.
LAR out-gained PHI 415-172 but nearly lost to its own mistakes. PHI's 68 net passing yards were a 23-year regular-season low.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: LAR C+: Stafford 13/17 for 149 in the 4th saved a bad game. PHI C: worst offensive performance since 2014.

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: Stafford now has 6 INTs (8 all last season) and looks uncomfortable behind his line.

takeaways.author: Kevin Patra
takeaways.text: Maye 269 yds, 3 TD despite two turnovers; late TD to Chism on a one-handed catch. BUF allowed 405 yds and 26 first downs. Doubs 2 TDs.
Winner Maye: 8 turnovers in his prior 13+ quarters, positive EPA for the first time since Week 18 last year.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: NE A-. BUF B-: James Cook got only 12 carries despite the matchup; the defense suddenly looks vulnerable.
BUF CB Maxwell Hairston allowed two TDs.

takeaways.author: Mike Reiss
takeaways.text: BUF secondary exposed in man coverage; Keon Coleman breakout.

takeaways.author: Dan Parr
takeaways.text: Bagent (first start in 3 years) 268 yds; Monangai 30-146-2 wore NYJ out. NYJ 0-for-7 on 3rd down. CHI has held three straight opponents to 12 or fewer.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: CHI A-: offense on the field 42+ minutes; NYJ never forced a punt. CHI 10-0 when rushing for 140+. NYJ D.

takeaways.author: Courtney Cronin, Rich Cimini
takeaways.text: NYJ had 99 yds before a late TD; identity crisis after three straight losses. Fitzpatrick's INT ended NYJ's 20-game interception drought.

takeaways.author: Bobby Kownack
takeaways.text: Lamar (2 TD, 144.2 rating at half) left with an ankle injury and BAL didn't score again under Huntley. Simpson's opening INT set up a TD. Ward-Tate 9-145 but mental errors and fumbles.

takeaways.author: Jamison Hensley, Turron Davenport
takeaways.text: Without Lamar: 98 yds and no points on 5 drives. Tyler Loop hit a 64-yd FG (stadium record).

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: Lamar: high-ankle sprain, day-to-day. Tate is the most productive Titans rookie WR game in 5+ years but fumbled twice.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: TEN C: failed on a drive to the BAL 2; three straight losses by 6 or fewer.

takeaways.author: Brooke Cersosimo
takeaways.text: Murray averaged 4.9 air yds per attempt (lowest by a Vikings QB in a season), 18.9% of throws 10+ air yds, no Jefferson. Hockenson 13/13-119. MIA's first four sacks of the year. Gordon 9-100 after Achane's injury; Dallas Turner at 5.5 sacks.
Loser: Murray/O'Connell. One offensive TD in 23 possessions over two games, against a weak MIA pass defense.
Reichard 5/5 FG, 28 straight makes; 27 of MIN's 71 season points.

takeaways.author: Kevin Seifert, Marcel Louis-Jacques
takeaways.text: MIN 4-0 despite the offense; defense held MIA to 8 first downs.

takeaways.author: Nick Wagoner, Jeff Legwold
takeaways.text: SF won without its peak offense; defense held DEN to 4.6 yds/play. Nix inaccurate (25/42, 214). Surtain's leg injury limits DEN's coverage flexibility.
SF 4-0; Purdy leads in EPA/dropback; first team with zero sacks allowed through four games since 2005.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: DEN C+: one first-half TD all season; secondary thin after losing both corners. SF B+.
Kittle's 56-yd TD (under a year post-Achilles) sealed it.

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: DEN injuries: Surtain, Riley Moss, Pat Bryant; DEN ranks 29th on offense and defense.

takeaways.author: Kevin Patra
takeaways.text: Walker 177 yds, 2 TD (76-yd run); Mahomes' 55-yd shot to Thornton set up the go-ahead score. Bassa's kickoff punch-out and five Araiza punts inside the 20 won the hidden-yardage battle. LV TEs (Bowers, Mayer, Thomas) 16-200-2.
Loser Kubiak: went for 4th-and-2 up 16-10, then kicked on 4th-and-1 down 3 with under 5:00 left.

takeaways.author: Nate Taylor
takeaways.text: KC has zero sacks in three weeks despite pass-rush investment; Thornton and Rice hurt. LV run game stuck (72 yds on 26 carries).

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: KC B, LV B: LV can play with anyone, but a late kick-return fumble hurt.

takeaways.author: Dan Parr
takeaways.text: SEA led 30-13 into the 4th and nearly gave it back; Nwosu's strip-sack of Herbert closed it. Darnold clean after two early INTs. Wilson 120 scrimmage yds, 2 TD with Price and Charbonnet out.
LAC 0-4, -39 point margin. Herbert 34.8 rating on downfield throws; Harbaugh-McDaniel disconnect.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: SEA B: three takeaways. LAC C: lost Alt and McConkey; Herbert sacked 4 times, 3 turnovers.

takeaways.author: Brady Henderson
takeaways.text: Herbert looked like himself after halftime.

takeaways.author: Kassidy Hill & Darin Gantt
takeaways.text: Young 29/41, 329, 2 TD, 0 INT, 11 straight completions to open; leads the NFL in passing yds. McMillan 14-192-2 (first Panther with 10+/175+/2 TD). Hubbard 20-122-2. CAR's 121 points through four weeks is a franchise record.
Winner Young: career-high 0.22 EPA/dropback despite missing linemen.

takeaways.author: John Breech
takeaways.text: DET C: allowed seven straight scoring drives; no pressure on Young. CAR A-.

takeaways.author: Brent Sobleski
takeaways.text: DET is allowing 31.8 PPG, third-most over 40 years; TeSlaa 95 yds.

takeaways.author: Garrett Podell
takeaways.text: ATL's line won the trenches: Bijan 19-145-2 and Brian Robinson Jr. 3 short TDs; NO had no answer for the run. Penix efficient (15/20, 223, 1 TD to Dotson). Shough threw for 286 but NO couldn't keep pace; Kamara's 2 TDs came on 7 carries. ATL 2-2, NO 1-3.
ATL's five rushing TDs matched the franchise record (headline).
ATL's second straight win; NO's front generated little pressure and gave up explosive plays.

league.text: Officials threw 238 flags for 1,830 yards across 14 games; on pace for the most penalized season.
Officiating flashpoints: Vrabel's unsportsmanlike flag, an exchange with Trey McBride, a referee confronting Eric Wilson.
